questions.question: Describe how can you recognize that a function belongs to a class.
questions.solution_html:
• Describe how you can recognize that a function belongs to a class.

  • It is declared inside the class definition.
  • Accessed using the dot (.) operator with an object.
  • Example: object.functionName();

questions.question: Examine how 2-D array can be represented in memory.
questions.solution_html:
• Examine how 2-D array can be represented in memory.
  • Stored in row-major order (row by row in continuous memory).
  • Example:
  • int a[2][3] = {{1,2,3},{4,5,6}};
  • Memory representation:
  • a[0][0], a[0][1], a[0][2], a[1][0], a[1][1], a[1][2]
  • Address formula:
  • Address(a[j]) = Base + ((i * totalColumns) + j) * size_of_element

questions.question: Compare friend function and a member function.
questions.solution_html:
• Compare friend function and member function.
  • Friend Function
  • Declared using friend keyword.
  • Not a member of the class but can access private data.
  • Invoked like a normal function.
  • Member Function
  • Declared normally inside class.
  • Is a member and can access all members directly.
  • Invoked using object and dot operator.

questions.question: Why is virtual base class is used?
questions.solution_html:
• Why is virtual base class used?
  • To avoid ambiguity in multiple inheritance (diamond problem). Ensures only one copy of
  • base class is inherited by all derived classes.
  • Example:
  • class A{}; class B: virtual public A{}; class C: virtual public A{}; class D: public
  • B, public C{};

questions.question: Write any two rules of operator overloading. [1x10 = 10]
questions.solution_html:
• Write any two rules of operator overloading.
  • - Only existing operators can be overloaded.
  • - At least one operand must be a user-defined type.
  • - Precedence/associativity of operators cannot change.
  • - Some operators like '.', '?:', 'sizeof' cannot be
  • overloaded.

  • show(); };

questions.question: Write two C++ programs to swap the values of two numbers: one using call by value and the other using call by reference. Analyze the differences in the outputs and explain why the results differ between the two methods.
questions.solution_html:
• Swapping using call by value and call by
  • reference:
  • Call by Value:
  • void swap(int a, int b){ int t=a; a=b; b=t; } // No change in originals
  • Call by Reference:
  • void swap(int &a;, int &b;){ int t=a; a=b; b=t; } // Changes
  • originals
  • Difference: Value uses copies; Reference uses actual
  • variables.
